newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Santos port faces possible 24-hour strike.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Santos port faces possible 24-hour strike.

text.p: Administrative portworkers at Brazil's Santos port are to hold an assembly on October 17 to decide whether to go on a 24-hour strike in protest over the privatisation of the container terminal, a port spokesman said.
The workers are angry at an announcement on September 30 the terminal is to be included in a number of areas which are being leased out to the private sector, he added.
"The problem is it was agreed with the Transport Minister Odacir Klein that all leasing programs would first be discussed with the unions," the spokesman said.
The assembly, to be held at 2000 local/2200 GMT, will decide whether to strike on October 18, the day of the first public audience on the leasing of the container terminal.
Some 20 areas within the port have been set aside for possible leasing, and three have already been contracted, including an area in which Cargill intends to build a sugar terminal.
The Administrative Portworkers' Union is one of the largest at the port and a strike by union members would effectively bring almost all operations to a halt, the spokesman said.
-- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
